title: Algorithmic Fidelity of Large Language Models in Generating Synthetic German Public Opinions: A Case Study

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with personas affiliated with different German political parties (e.g., The Left, The Greens, AfD) and comparing the distribution of their open-ended survey responses to actual human data from the German Longitudinal Election Studies (GLES) using Jensen-Shannon Divergence and Information Gain.

Evaluating algorithmic fidelity by prompting LLMs with personas of varying educational and vocational backgrounds, and measuring the divergence of their generated opinions from real survey data to detect over- or under-representation of educated groups.

Prompting models with personas from different age cohorts (18-29, 30-44, 45-59, 60+) and assessing how accurately the generated public opinions align with age-specific responses in the GLES survey data.
Comparing the distribution of LLM-generated survey responses for personas located in East versus West Germany against real regional survey distributions to identify geographic representation gaps.
Prompting models with male and female personas to evaluate the alignment of the generated synthetic opinions with gender-specific human survey data.
